note: Clean pass with caveats. Source is the EANNA 2023 deposit itself (BIDAT dataset e3ceb7aa-95a8-4838-909b-155719847d21, licence 'Creative Commons Attribution'; Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia, fieldwork by INE). MAPPING: the codebook 'Libro de codigos base de datos EANNA 2023' (sha256 0478c51b7101a71a5a70f1219f1d17e4752f9cff1d0e50ab98118e02e547306a), sheet '2. Cuidador(a) Principal', and the deposit .dta's own labels tie every variable NAME to a label and to value labels 1='Si'/2='No' for all 30 variables. WORDS: the administered caregiver questionnaire 'Cuestionario_Cuidador_Principal_EANNA_2023.pdf' (sha256 5023fd0a93e16a3ea15e0f38045fe17cbe0f873470378301e22087739cc43ada), Modulo: Acontecimientos; its preface states that response alternatives are numbered with the value stored in the database. The codebook's variable labels are abbreviated (e.g. ac1_1 'Desastre afecto a su hogar 12 meses: Sequia'), so the shipped wording is the questionnaire's, not the label's; the show-card deck (Tarjetero_EANNA_2023.pdf, cards 'Desastres Naturales', 'Problemas en el hogar', 'Acciones tomadas') prints the same stems and alternatives verbatim. (1) Code derivation: the do-file keeps rp2==1 (the selected child's primary caregiver) and writes `gen item = "`var'"`, so `item` IS the source Stata variable name (exempt pattern); the table is the `strpos(item,"a")==1` split of the caregiver block, i.e. the ac* module. Checked against the data anyway by re-running the do-file's filter over the deposit .dta: all 60 item x value cells match live counts exactly (server-side GROUP BY, no export), and all 30 Si/No profiles are distinct, so every item is distinguished from every other, including inside the ac1/ac2 (n=17631), ac5 (n=5035) and ac6 (n=506) blocks. (2) Shape: ac1, ac2, ac5 and ac6 are shown-card batteries of separate Si/No questions sharing one read-out stem; the stem is in section_prompt and each alternative is item_text. ac3 is a single question in its own section with blank section_prompt. No module- or questionnaire-level respondent introduction exists for this module, so instructions is blank. Interviewer-only text (the 'Muestre tarjeta ...' card prompts, skip instructions, 'Condicion habilitante' lines) is not shipped. (3) Skip structure, disclosed because the per-item n differ by design: ac3 is asked only if any ac1/ac2 = Si (live n 8245); ac5_* only if ac3 = Si (n 5035 = ac3's 5035 Si); ac6_* only if ac5_8 = Si (n 506 = ac5_8's 506 Si). 28 caregivers are -98 'Sin Dato' on ac1/ac2 (17659 ids vs n 17631). The live table carries the skipped cells as rows with missing resp: 234,407 of 529,770 rows. (4) RESPONSE-DATA FINDING: these are household-level questions ('Nivel: hogar'), but the deposit is organised by selected child (folio), and the do-file keeps one caregiver row per folio. The 17,659 live ids are 17,659 folios from only 13,867 households and 14,056 distinct (household, person) caregivers; in 3,311 households with more than one folio (7,103 rows) the ac* answer vectors are identical across folios in 3,311 of 3,311 households. So 3,792 ids are repeats of another id's household answers -- a copies-not-design duplication. Not fixable in item text; flagged for the response table. (5) Language: administered in Spanish, which ships in the base fields. The deposit has no English version, so the _translated columns are IRW's own translation (translation_source=machine_translation); public_note written. (6) Transcription: verbatim from the questionnaire, including its own wording 'perdida de ingresos bienes o patrimonio' (no comma) in ac3; ac6_2's codebook label abbreviates 'educ. superior' where the questionnaire reads 'educacion superior' -- the questionnaire ships. (7) Rights: no clause reserving a right is locatable. The instrument is the Chilean state's own survey questionnaire, published in full by the agency alongside a CC BY dataset; no fee, non-commercial term or redistribution bar is stated. No register row written. (8) Step 3b: the dictionary Description ('primary caregiver ... whether unexpected events like natural disasters affected their lives') matches the live items. (9) irw-validate reports name_length ERROR (43 characters vs the 40-character cap) and name_charset WARN (hyphens). Both are properties of the pre-existing response table's NAME (irw#2365), not of this item text; `table` must reproduce the live name for the join, so it was left as published.

Clean pass with caveats. Source is the EANNA 2023 deposit itself (BIDAT dataset e3ceb7aa-95a8-4838-909b-155719847d21, licence 'Creative Commons Attribution', Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia; fieldwork by INE). WORDS: the administered caregiver questionnaire 'Cuestionario_Cuidador_Principal_EANNA_2023.pdf' (sha256 5023fd0a93e16a3ea15e0f38045fe17cbe0f873470378301e22087739cc43ada), 'Modulo: Cuidador(a) principal del NNA', pp. 37-43, questions cp2-cp9. MAPPING: the codebook 'Libro de codigos base de datos EANNA 2023' (sha256 0478c51b7101a71a5a70f1219f1d17e4752f9cff1d0e50ab98118e02e547306a), sheet '2. Cuidador(a) Principal', and the deposit .dta's own variable labels (42/42 present, identical to the codebook's), tie every variable NAME to its label and value labels. The questionnaire's front matter also states 'Las alternativas de respuesta se encuentran numeradas y coinciden con el valor que aparece en la base de datos'. (1) Code derivation: data/chile_2023_children-adolescents-survey.do writes gen item = "`var'" over the source columns, so `item` IS the Stata variable name (exempt pattern); this table is the do-file's 'keep if strpos(item,"c")==1' split of the Cuidador(a) Principal block (rp2==1). Checked against the data anyway by route 9 (verify script): 94/94 categorical item x value cells reproduce the codebook frequencies exactly, all 34 categorical frequency profiles distinct; the cp9_* 'No sabe' counts 52/64/85/101 match; and cp7_*/cp9_* live means reproduce, to 4 decimals, the means obtained by applying the do-file's hh:mm conversion to the deposit .dta (cp7_1 11.7493, cp7_2 1.9054, cp7_3 0.1387, cp7_4 0.0224; cp9_1 1.9228 ... cp9_4 0.7551). (2) Shape: cp2 is a multiple-select ('Registre todas las alternativas que correspondan') stored as one 0/1 column per alternative; its stem is section_prompt, each alternative is item_text, option_text is the codebook's 0='No'/1='Si'. cp5, cp6, cp7, cp8, cp9 are batteries whose shared stem is section_prompt; the cp5 prompt also carries the two static texts read immediately before it (cp_texto2, cp5_texto). cp3 and cp4 are single questions with blank section_prompt. instructions = the module opener cp_texto1. (3) cp7_* (hours/week) and cp9_* (hours/day) are free numeric entries recorded as hh:mm and converted by the do-file to decimal hours rounded to 0.1; they get one row per observed live value with option_text blank (not padded), 239 rows. (4) RESPONSE-DATA FINDING, cp9_*: the questionnaire instructs 'Si no sabe registre 88:88' and the codebook labels 88:88 'No sabe'; the do-file's mvdecode catches -88/-99/-98/77/87 but not the string '88:88', which its hh:mm conversion turns into 88+88/60 = 89.47 -> 89.5. So resp=89.5 in cp9_1..cp9_4 (52/64/85/101 respondents) is the 'don't know' code, not 89.5 hours, on an item the questionnaire caps at 8 hours. Shipped as option_text 'No sabe' for resp 89.5. It moves the means a lot: excluding it, cp9_1..cp9_4 means are 1.662/1.236/0.613/0.240 vs 1.923/1.559/1.044/0.755 with it (cp9_4 x3.1). Should be recoded to missing in the response table. (5) RESPONSE-DATA FINDING, cp2_1..cp2_9 (present in the deposit itself, not introduced by IRW): of the 8,793 caregivers routed to cp2, 3,493 (39.7%) have ALL NINE reasons 1-9 marked 1, 5,115 have none of them, 179 exactly one, 4 two, 2 three (server-side count on the live table). Per-item 'Si' counts are therefore near-identical (3,493-3,573) and the nine columns intercorrelate 0.97-1.00 in the .dta. For a spontaneous-response question ('Espere respuesta espontanea y clasifique') this is not a plausible response pattern; it looks like an export/coding fault in the source file. cp2_10 (191) and cp2_77 (131) do not share it. The codebook prints the same counts, so the live table faithfully reproduces the deposit. The item text is correct for the question asked; the responses to cp2_1..cp2_9 should not be analysed as recorded. (6) RESPONSE-DATA NOTE: the live resp values carry float32 artefacts from Stata's float storage (0.30000001, 0.69999999, 3.5999999, 4.1999998, 6.1999998 etc.). The items CSV reproduces them exactly (validate_items.R required it); a join that rounds resp to 0.3 will miss those rows. (7) Stripped from shipped text and disclosed here: interviewer-facing blue text ('Espere respuesta espontanea y clasifique', 'Registre todas las alternativas que correspondan', 'Muestre tarjeta ...', 'Lea alternativas', the hh:mm entry instructions 'Registre en formato horas y minutos (hh:mm)... Si cree que no deberia trabajar registre 00:00', 'La cifra no puede ser mayor a 8 horas al dia'), and 'Especifique' from cp2_77's '77. Otra razon. Especifique' (shipped 'Otra razon'). cp2_1 ships the questionnaire's 'Para ayudar en los gastos...' (the codebook label drops 'Para'); cp8_5 ships the questionnaire's 'hermanos(as)' (codebook 'hermanos'). The cp7/cp9 hh:mm examples in the questionnaire (cp7's example refers to 'sabado y domingo', a copy-paste artefact) are interviewer notes and were not shipped. (8) Language Spanish in the base fields; no English version exists in the deposit, so the _translated columns are IRW's own translation (translation_source=machine_translation); public_note written. (9) Rights: no clause reserving a right is locatable in the questionnaire PDF (grep for derech/licen/copyright/reproduc/prohib/autoriz returns only survey content) or the deposit page; the instrument is the Chilean state's own survey questionnaire published by the agency that owns it alongside a CC BY dataset. No register row written. (10) Step 3b: dictionary Description is survey-wide; the live items are the caregiver's own work history and opinions on child/adolescent work (cp2-cp9). cp1 (age at first job) is a covariate (cov_age_first_job), not an item. Note cp2/cp3 were only asked of caregivers who started work before 18 (n 8,793/8,781 vs ~17,500 for cp4-cp9). (11) irw-validate: ERROR name_length (43 chars vs the 40-char cap) and WARN name_charset (hyphens) are properties of the pre-existing response table name (irw#2365); the `table` column must reproduce it exactly, so nothing was renamed. | Step 5c (orchestrator): audit_batch WARN '70.9% of rows have blank option_text; cp7_1..cp7_4 have no option_text rows' is EXPECTED, not an itemtext defect: cp7_*/cp9_* are hh:mm hours-of-care items converted to decimal hours by the .do file, so each observed value gets its own row with option_text blank (never padded with its own number). cp9_* have one labelled row each (89.5 = 'No sabe', the '88:88' code the .do file failed to decode -- a RESPONSE-DATA defect, orchestrator re-checked: 52/64/85/101 rows at 89.5 on cp9_1..4, means 1.92/1.56/1.04/0.76 with vs 1.66/1.24/0.61/0.24 without); cp7_* have no such code, hence no labelled rows. Also re-checked the cp2_1..cp2_9 finding: of 8,793 ids with any cp2_1..9 response, 3,493 mark all nine =1, 5,115 none, 179/4/2 mark 1/2/3.

Clean pass with caveats. (1) Code derivation: data/chile_2023_children-adolescents-survey.do (self-administered block, `keep if responde_autoaplicado == 1`) writes `gen item = "`var'"`, so `item` IS the source Stata variable name (g1_1..g1_8) -- the exempt pattern; mapping_basis=data_labels. The MAPPING comes from the codebook 'Libro de codigos base de datos EANNA 2023' (sha256 0478c51b7101a71a5a70f1219f1d17e4752f9cff1d0e50ab98118e02e547306a), sheet '5. Autoaplicado', which gives each g1_* variable its label and value labels 1=Nunca, 2=Pocas veces, 3=Casi siempre, 4=Siempre, -98=Sin Dato; the variable labels are identical to the questionnaire stems. The WORDS come from the administered questionnaire 'Cuestionario_Autoaplicado_NNA_9_a_17_anos_EANNA_2023.pdf' (sha256 03adf04fe0c7d0a11d58421b538d86403136649dbdd7f2b8f29cd450f634ea59), Modulo: ECLIS, which prints each question with its variable name (e.g. 'g1_1. Mis companeros(as) se burlan de mi') and states 'Las alternativas de respuesta se encuentra numeradas y coinciden con el valor que aparece en la base de datos'. (2) Checked against the data anyway by route 9: a server-side GROUP BY item,resp on the live table reproduces all 32 of 32 item x value frequencies printed in the codebook exactly (e.g. g1_1 9030/2855/363/127; g1_3 322/1311/4078/6665; g1_8 3613/4864/2392/1507); all 8 profiles are distinct. Scratch script only (.cache/.../freqcheck.R); no verify_ script written, per the template's data_labels exemption. (3) instructions = the module's static text 'A continuacion, tienes que leer una serie de afirmaciones acerca de ti en el colegio...' (no terminal period in the source; none added). Interviewer/programming notes ('Tipo de pregunta', 'Condicion habilitante: esta asistiendo al colegio...') are not shipped. Single trivial section. (4) Language: administered in Spanish (self-completed on a tablet); Spanish ships in the base fields. No English version exists in the deposit, so the _translated columns are IRW's own translation (translation_source=machine_translation). (5) Instrument identity (Step 3b): the dictionary Description names the survey generally; the module is ECLIS, and these eight items are the 8-item bullying sub-scale of the Escala de Clima Social Escolar (Aron, Milicic & Armijo 2012, Figura 2 'Items asociados a bullying': items 37, 38, 39, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45), with EANNA adding gender-inclusive '(as)' forms and minor rewording ('La paso bien con mis companeros en clase' -> 'Lo paso bien con mis companeros(as) de clase'; 'La paso mal en la sala clase' -> 'La paso mal en la sala de clase'). Per that paper g1_3 (item 39) is keyed opposite to the other seven; the IRW table stores raw 1-4 (Nunca..Siempre) for all eight, as the codebook frequencies confirm. (6) Rights: no clause reserving a right is locatable. The words shipped are the Chilean state's own questionnaire, published with a CC BY dataset; the originating ECLIS article (Universitas Psychologica, via Redalyc open access, pdf sha256 1054e8efcd7ebc07f50efa36c119d4ada81ad8bccd9e46224746138eacea9df1) prints the items and states no fee, permission, non-commercial or no-redistribution term; a web search for ECLIS use/permission terms found none. Silence is permission. A commercial book by the same authors (Aron & Milicic, 'Clima Social Escolar. Escalas para su evaluacion') exists; its terms were not examined. No register row written (a round may never write ship/ship_with_note). (7) Response-data observation: the live table has 99,888 rows = 8 items x 12,486 respondents, but non-missing n per item is 12,375-12,376. The codebook counts 9 or 8 'Sin Dato' (-98) per item; the remaining ~102 per item are respondents routed past G1 by the 'currently attending school' filter, kept as NA-resp rows. Not a defect of the item text. (8) irw-validate WARNs name_charset on the hyphens in the pre-existing table name (irw#2365); the `table` column must reproduce the live name, so it was left as published.
